source: Native AWS via scripts/aws/aws_cli.py run/result; default authorized credentials

primary_reference_semantics.DeleteTopic: Deletes a topic and all its subscriptions; may prevent prior messages from delivery; deleting a nonexistent topic is idempotent.
primary_reference_semantics.Subscribe: Subscribes endpoint; same-account SQS does not require endpoint confirmation; ReturnSubscriptionArn requests ARN even if pending.
primary_reference_semantics.Unsubscribe: Deletes a subscription; authenticated deletion can require subscription/topic owner. Requests here are signed owner calls, not UnsubscribeURL HTTP requests.

findings.finding: DeleteTopic succeeded. Exact-topic GetTopicAttributes and ListSubscriptionsByTopic returned NotFound/404 at all four scheduled intervals; the old subscription attributes remained Success/200, with its reads completing 2.092, 7.179, 17.189 and 32.353 seconds after DeleteTopic completed.
findings.interpretation_boundary: Retained metadata visibility is observed, not a claim that asynchronous cascade never completes.

findings.finding: Repeating DeleteTopic while absent succeeded. Recreating the same owned name completed 34.078 seconds after deletion and returned the identical topic ARN. Recreated topic membership was an empty Subscriptions array, without NextToken, while the old subscription attributes remained readable.

The retained old subscription was not merely inert metadata in this observation: before any resubscribe, a fresh publish to the recreated ARN delivered to SQS, carrying the old subscription ARN in the native UnsubscribeURL. Its SNS MessageId matched that fresh Publish response, excluding an old queued positive-control message. Receive completed 37.796 seconds after deletion, 0.841 seconds after Publish completed.
findings.timing_boundary: Six receives covered 30.431 seconds in this phase. One owned subscription delivery was observed; no claim about behavior after longer recreation delays.

findings.finding: Subscribe to the same endpoint after recreation returned a different subscription ARN. ListSubscriptionsByTopic contained only the new ARN, while both old and new attributes returned Success. One fresh Publish delivered two SQS notifications with the same SNS MessageId: first the new ARN and then the old ARN in their respective native UnsubscribeURLs. This distinguishes two subscription deliveries from an ordinary duplicate carrying one subscription identity.
findings.timing_boundary: Seven receives covered 31.830 seconds. The new and old deliveries completed 72.669 and 74.185 seconds after topic deletion.

findings.finding: Explicitly unsubscribing the old ARN succeeded and made its attributes NotFound; current membership and attributes remained intact. A subsequent fresh Publish delivered using the new ARN.
findings.timing_boundary: Three receives covered 12.974 seconds after this publish and observed only the new subscription identity. This is bounded absence of an old-identity delivery, not a guarantee against arbitrarily late deliveries.

findings.finding: Explicit current Unsubscribe succeeded, its GetSubscriptionAttributes became NotFound, and exact-topic membership became empty. Repeated Unsubscribe succeeded. Finally both owned subscription ARNs and topic returned NotFound, and the owned queue returned AWS.SimpleQueueService.NonExistentQueue. All five consumed messages were explicitly deleted.
findings.resource_and_call_counts: One unique topic name, two topic incarnations with identical ARN, one queue, two unique subscription ARNs, four publishes, five deliveries, 75 API calls; total native experiment including cleanup 149.933 seconds.

result.message: The specified queue does not exist.

limitations: Single owned standard topic name and same-account standard SQS queue in one native account/region.
Non-delivery is bounded observation, not a guarantee against later retries or asynchronous cleanup.
No conclusion about long-term retained metadata lifetime; explicit Unsubscribe in this probe ends observation.
No global subscription/topic inventory; only exact owned topic lists and exact subscription attribute reads.
Original SQS Body strings containing signed SNS envelopes are retained unchanged; decoded delivery identity is separate derived data.
CLI debug is held transiently only to extract native HTTP status; raw debug/signing headers are discarded.

The local five-minute retained-subscription cleanup deadline is uncalibrated. Replay advances only through measured native request timestamps (old/new deliveries completed 72.669/74.185 seconds after deletion); it neither tests nor presents five minutes as AWS behavior.
